meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мочь'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to help', paired with 'помогать'.

examples.text: Экскаваторщик — это не мой уровень. Может, поможешь?
examples.trans: Excavator driver isn't my level. Maybe you could help?

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'your', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?
Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.trans: They called from the Italian restaurant.
In the evening they went to a restaurant.

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'жинать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to dine'.

examples.trans: The oligarch will dine with us?

examples.text: Завтра в вашем ресторане будет ужинать мой босс.
examples.trans: Tomorrow my boss will be having dinner at your restaurant.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'my, mine', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Borrowed from English 'boss' (from Dutch 'baas', master).

examples.trans: It will be done, my boss.
Just to spite you and your boss.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes, indeed', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'амый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('the most; the very').

examples.trans: The most important thing is the people.
Do you know the main thing?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big, large').

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'honour; (Ваша честь) Your Honour' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ваша честь, у нас есть заявление.
examples.trans: Your Honour, we have a statement.
It is a matter of honour.

examples.text: Ваша честь, у нас есть важное заявление.
examples.trans: Your Honour, we have an important statement.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('any').

examples.text: Любая обезьяна эти выборы выиграет! Ты что, хуже обезьяны?
examples.trans: Any monkey will win this election! What, are you worse than a monkey?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'where', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).

examples.trans: And the kitchen is over there.
We are sitting in the kitchen.

examples.text: Проходите, пожалуйста! Как видите, большой коридор, а там кухня.
examples.trans: Come on in, please! As you can see, a big hall, and the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'to, towards', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ожаление'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'regret, pity' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Вы, к сожалению, не в моём вкусе.
examples.trans: Unfortunately, you are not my type.

examples.text: Я бы рад вам помочь. Но вы, к сожалению, не в моём вкусе.
examples.trans: I would be glad to help you. But unfortunately you are not my type.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'very, very much', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'нятый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('busy; occupied, taken').
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'something; somehow', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'well; come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'all right, OK', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nothing', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'трашный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('terrible, scary').

examples.text: Ничего страшного. Теперь мы одна команда.
examples.trans: Nothing serious. Now we're one team.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'something, anything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Правда, Нин, всё нормально. Скажи что-нибудь, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Honestly, Nina, everything's fine. Say something, please.
Are you doing anything about it?

придумать.gloss: to think up, to come up with

meanings.en: to think up, to come up with
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'думать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to think up, to come up with', paired with 'придумывать'.

examples.trans: You came up with this yourself!

examples.text: Как нет? Ты же сам это всё придумал!
examples.trans: What do you mean, no time? You came up with all this yourself!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'until, before; up to', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

related.gloss: to reach, walk as far as

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'видание'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'meeting; date' in everyday Russian.
